turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I'm here because of this issue I have with elevators. I mean, I know they aren't really dangerous, but when I have to actually get in one, I just get scared... like I'm going to be trapped in there. I just can't seem to make myself feel normal about it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an intense, disproportionate fear of a specific situation (elevators), acknowledging they are not actually dangerous but feeling terrified of being trapped.
symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient states that actually getting into an elevator immediately provokes fear.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever experience sudden waves of intense fear or panic out of the blue, without any obvious trigger?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's only when I have to deal with elevators. If I don't have to get in one, I feel totally fine. I don't just get scared for no reason out of nowhere.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient states they only experience intense fear or panic when dealing with a specific situation, which is elevators.

turns.doctor_question: Besides elevators, do you feel this same kind of fear in other situations, such as on public transportation, in open spaces, or in crowded places?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just the elevators. I take the bus to work every day, and that's fine. Crowds and open spaces don't bother me at all. It's just... getting into an elevator. That's the only thing that sets it off.
